title: Albanian Riviera Road Trip: The Best Beaches from Vlorë to Ksamil by Car
metaTitle: Albanian Riviera Road Trip: Best Beaches by Car
metaDescription: Plan an Albanian Riviera road trip: the best beaches from Vlorë to Ksamil, with access, parking notes and the best season to go. Start planning your route.
excerpt: A beach-by-beach guide to the Albanian Riviera by car, from Dhërmi and Jalë to Himarë, Borsh and Ksamil, with access and parking tips and the best time to go.
html:
The Albanian Riviera is the stretch of Ionian coast between Vlorë and Ksamil, and it is best explored by car. One coastal road connects almost every beach, so you can swim at a different bay every day, stop at viewpoints and reach places that buses skip. This guide covers the best beaches in Albania along that road, from north to south, with notes on access, parking and the best season to go.

Planning your Albanian Riviera road trip

The coastal road from Vlorë to Saranda is roughly 120 to 130 km, but it is winding, so the full stretch takes around four hours without stops. Most travellers spend three to five days here, basing themselves in one or two places. Dhërmi or Himarë works well in the north, and Saranda or Ksamil in the south.

  • Getting there from Tirana: Vlorë is about two to two and a half hours from Tirana airport. See our guide to driving from Tirana to Ksamil and Saranda for both route options.
  • Which car: a compact car is easiest on narrow roads and in tight beach car parks. If you want to explore steep gravel tracks to quieter coves, a rental SUV gives more ground clearance.
  • Beach type: most Riviera beaches are pebble or fine shingle with very clear water. Water shoes are useful.

Best season for the Riviera

PeriodWhat to expect
MayGreen landscapes, quiet beaches, sea still fresh for swimming
JuneWarm sea, long days, beach bars open, manageable crowds
July–AugustHot, busy and lively; traffic and parking are hardest
SeptemberWarm sea, fewer people, often the best balance
OctoberQuieter, some places closing, swimming still possible on warm days

If your dates are flexible, June and September offer the best mix of warm water and easy driving.

The Llogara Pass: gateway to the Riviera

South of Vlorë and Orikum, the road climbs through pine forest to the Llogara Pass. At the top, the whole Riviera opens up below you. It is a good place for a coffee and photos before the descent. The hairpins down the other side are steep, so use a low gear and take your time. Our guide to driving in Albania has more tips for mountain roads.

The best Albanian Riviera beaches, north to south

Dhërmi

Dhërmi is one of the Riviera's most popular resorts, with a long beach, beach bars and plenty of accommodation. The old village sits on the hillside above the road, while the beach lies below. Further along, the Drymades area offers a long stretch of beach backed by olive trees. Access and parking: roads lead down from the main road to the beach areas. In summer, paid parking near the beach is common.

Jalë

Jalë is a small bay with clear turquoise water, surrounded by hills between Dhërmi and Himarë. It is one of the prettiest beaches on the coast, with sunbeds and a few restaurants. Access and parking: a steep, narrow road leads down from the main road near Vuno. Drive carefully, especially in a larger car, and expect limited parking in high season.

Gjipe (hike-in or boat)

Gjipe is a beautiful beach at the mouth of a canyon, and its remoteness keeps it relatively unspoilt. You cannot drive all the way to the sand. Access: a side road from the main road leads to a parking area above the beach. From there it is a downhill walk of roughly 20 to 30 minutes on a rough path, and longer coming back up in the heat. Wear proper shoes and bring plenty of water. Boat trips from nearby beaches are an alternative in summer.

Himarë and Livadh

Himarë is a relaxed town with a small promenade, restaurants and an old castle quarter on the hill above. Livadh beach, just north of the town, is a long beach that is popular with families. Other small beaches are within a short drive. Access and parking: easy, with parking in town and near Livadh, though spaces fill up on summer afternoons. Himarë is a good base for exploring the middle of the Riviera.

Porto Palermo

Porto Palermo is a quiet, sheltered bay with a small fortress, associated with Ali Pasha of Tepelena, on a peninsula. The water is calm and clear, and the castle makes a good short stop. Access and parking: the bay is right beside the main road south of Himarë, with space to park near the fortress.

Borsh

Borsh has one of the longest beaches on the Albanian Riviera, several kilometres of pebble shore backed by olive groves. Even in summer you can usually find a quiet spot. Access and parking: very easy, as a road runs parallel to the beach with plenty of places to stop. The ruins of Borsh castle stand on the hill above the village.

Lukovë

Lukovë is a hillside village above a series of quiet bays. The beaches below are less developed than those further north and are ideal if you want peace. Access and parking: side roads lead from the main road down to the coast. Some are narrow or unpaved in places, so a higher car helps.

Ksamil

Ksamil, south of Saranda, is famous for its turquoise water, small islands and fine pale beaches. It is the busiest spot on the coast in summer, with beach clubs and restaurants lining the shore, and Butrint National Park is just a few kilometres away. Access and parking: traffic and parking are challenging in July and August. Book accommodation with parking, arrive before mid-morning and walk between beaches.

Sample 4-day Riviera plan by car

  1. Day 1: Vlorë to Dhërmi via the Llogara Pass. Afternoon swim in Dhërmi.
  2. Day 2: Morning at Jalë, afternoon hike down to Gjipe. Overnight in Dhërmi or Himarë.
  3. Day 3: Himarë and Livadh, Porto Palermo, then Borsh. Continue to Saranda or Ksamil.
  4. Day 4: Butrint in the morning and Ksamil's beaches in the afternoon.

To combine the coast with Berat and Gjirokastër, see our full Albania road trip itinerary.

Practical tips for beach-hopping by car

  • Carry cash in lek for parking, sunbeds and small beach restaurants.
  • Do not leave valuables visible in the car while you swim.
  • Watch for pedestrians on the main road in beach villages, especially in the evening.
  • Keep sand and wet towels under control: a beach mat in the boot helps keep the car clean.
  • Avoid driving the coast road after dark if you are not familiar with it.
  • Consider Super CDW, which removes the excess, for narrow roads and tight parking.

faq.question: What is the best beach on the Albanian Riviera?
faq.answer: It depends on what you want. Ksamil is famous for turquoise water and islands but is very busy in summer. Jalë is a small, picturesque bay, Gjipe is wild and reached on foot, and Borsh offers a long, uncrowded beach. Driving along the coast lets you try several and choose your favourite.

faq.question: Do you need a car to visit the Albanian Riviera?
faq.answer: You can reach the main towns by bus, but a car makes a big difference. Many of the best beaches, such as Jalë, Porto Palermo and the coves near Lukovë, are hard to reach by public transport. With a car you can also stop at viewpoints, start early and move on whenever a beach gets crowded.

faq.question: How do you get to Gjipe beach?
faq.answer: Gjipe cannot be reached by car. A side road from the main coastal road leads to a parking area above the beach, followed by a downhill walk of roughly 20 to 30 minutes on a rough path. The walk back up is harder in the heat. In summer, boat trips from nearby beaches are an alternative.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit the Albanian Riviera?
faq.answer: June and September are usually the best months: the sea is warm, the days are long and the roads and beaches are less crowded than in peak season. July and August are hot and lively but busy, with harder parking. May and October are quieter, with cooler water.
